title: First paint under 0.1 s: draw before geometry processing runs, and cut window startup
description:
Time to first paint in the quad-layout scene is about 1 s by the printed number and really about 8 s. Canvas3D.initGL prints 'Time to First Paint' before ModelScene.initGL calls initModel, which runs QuadLayoutEngine synchronously on the main thread (about 6.9 s on the default model) before IxdarWindow.loop paints anything. Headless prints a negative time because HeadlessPlatform.startTime is unset. Two parts. (A) Paint first: every scene that does geometry processing at load (QuadLayoutScene and every other ModelScene subclass or scene whose initModel/loadModel runs a pipeline: survey them all) must load and upload the plain input mesh, present a frame, and run the processing on a worker thread, then hand the result to the render thread for GL upload (the render thread owns the context; follow the processInputQueue pattern). Put the mechanism in ModelScene once so each scene opts in with little code; a reload from the model menu or the automation `model` route takes the same path, a newer request supersedes a running one, the scene shows that processing is in progress, and automation callers that wait for a scene to be ready (run-scene, sceneReady, screenshot) still wait for the processed result. (B) Window time: from main to 'Window Time' is 0.79 s in the user's F5 run: glfwInit 0.21 s, glfwCreateWindow 0.10 s, then 0.49 s to Window Time that is mostly off-CPU and not yet explained. Find where it goes with a wall-clock profile of a windowed (not headless) run, and cut it. Candidates: disable libdecor on Wayland (glfwInitHint GLFW_WAYLAND_LIBDECOR to disable; the log shows libdecor-gtk failing to init), skip glfwSetWindowPos on Wayland (it only raises GLFW_FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE), class loading in LwjglPlatform/LwjglGL (try a Java 26 AOT cache, -XX:AOTCacheOutput / -XX:AOTCache, and say whether launch.json should use it), the window icon load, and anything else on the path. Measure without the debugger and async-profiler agents attached, which the F5 entries add. Move the 'Time to First Paint' print to after the first glfwSwapBuffers on the render thread (and the headless equivalent) so the number means what it says. Goal: first frame under 0.1 s measured from main. Seven sibling CRAW tickets speed up each pipeline stage; this ticket owns no pipeline code. Related: CRAW-4 (cached layouts).

Round 2 (user request 2026-10-15), from a 1 ms wall profile of the eng-14 worktree's windowed launch (first paint 0.67-0.84 s): Terminal font ~180 ms (msdf atlas PNG decode via stb 66 ms + first-use Gson parse of the atlas JSON 38 ms + Terminal.<clinit> resources 20 ms); scene constructor ~150 ms (class loading 65 ms, JOML Options.<clinit> building a DecimalFormat that loads locale data 46 ms via Camera3D lookAt, reflective bindAutomationIfAvailable 17 ms); Scene.initGL 57 ms (Canvas3D.initPoints builds a shell, Camera2D and an SDFCircle with a shader compile that model scenes never draw); mesh upload 74 ms (HalfEdgeMesh radius/center/boundsMin/boundsMax recomputed repeatedly, runtime shader compile, 8 ms waiting on prefetch); LWJGL Callback/MemoryStack first use 69 ms; render thread's first frame ~175 ms of which ~130 ms is blocked in Mesa EGL inside the first glfwSwapBuffers waiting on the Hyprland compositor. The user asked for all of the fixes, and for the msdf-atlas-gen font atlas to move from JSON+PNG to a better structure (a compact binary of glyph metrics plus raw texel data that uploads without PNG decode or JSON parsing).
definition-of-done:
1. 'Time to First Paint' prints after the first presented frame, windowed and headless, and is positive in both. 2. quad-layout's first frame, showing the input mesh, is under 0.1 s from main in a plain (no debugger, no profiler) windowed run, or the report states the measured floor and what is left. 3. Every scene that processes geometry at load paints the input before processing; changes-made lists which scenes those are. 4. The processed result appears without user action when processing finishes; a second model load during processing supersedes the first. 5. run-scene and screenshot on quad-layout still capture the finished layout. 6. The 0.49 s between window creation and Window Time is accounted for in changes-made. 7. `ixd wt done` passes.

The two 'Time to First Paint' println lines in IxdarWindow (windowed render thread after the first glfwSwapBuffers, headless after the first paintGL) are the DoD-1 number and stay.

5. Whole-suite check: `python3 /home/acw/Code/Ixdar/tmp/quad-suite/run_suite.py --checkout <this worktree> --out /home/acw/Code/Ixdar/tmp/quad-suite/<ticket> --compare /home/acw/Code/Ixdar/tmp/quad-suite/master-0f52d26f` covers sphere_base, sphere_random, bolt, hand, fandisk, elk, feline, fertility, botijo, block, Hand-tri-30k, rockerarm, buddha and the crawfish scan (~/crawfish/IMG_4109.glb, 8 GB heap). Every mesh reports MATCH against the master baseline: the same status (a mesh master fails on must fail the same way), the same count signature, and an identical screenshot. The per-mesh stage times before/after go in changes-made. A DIFF stops for a user ruling.

Those two lines are `System.out.println(FIRST_PAINT_LABEL + (Clock.time() - startTime))` in IxdarWindow.loop and IxdarWindow.runHeadless.

Round 2: each of the five profile items is addressed and re-measured with a 1 ms wall profile of a plain windowed launch (median of 3, first paint and per-item times before/after); the font atlas loads from the new binary format with text pixel-identical to master; the compositor's share of the first swap is measured and stated.

FontAtlasBinary.main, the atlas converter run by 'mvn -q -pl ixdar-app exec:java@compile-font-atlas', prints one summary line on stdout: '<path> is up to date' or 'wrote <path> (<n> bytes)'.
testing-plan: 1. Plain windowed launch of quad-layout, 3 runs, before and after; record each timer line. 2. Wall-clock async-profiler capture of a windowed launch (event=wall). 3. run-scene + screenshot for quad-layout and each converted scene; image-diff against master. 4. Load a second model through the automation model route while the first is processing. 5. mvn test for touched packages.
unknowns: Which scenes besides QuadLayoutScene process geometry at load
How scenes that read halfEdgeMesh during processing avoid racing the worker thread
Whether an AOT cache is worth wiring into launch.json
changes-made: Relaunch state (agent 2): worktree diff has ModelScene.processLoadedModel/processInBackground (worker thread, serial supersede, render-thread install step, 'processing <model> ... s' label, isSceneReady() false while processing), initial-model prefetch on a worker, Screenshot/MultiviewScreenshot awaitSceneReady, Health uses isSceneReady, Platform.runInBackground (+3 impls), lazy Manifold boolean backend, automation server started off render thread, libdecor disabled + Wayland skips icon/window pos, LWJGL hash checks off, first-paint print after first swap. Converted: QuadLayout, CrossFieldExamination, MotorcycleGraphExamination, ParametrizationExamination, EmbeddedTMesh, MeshNodeViewer, MeshBoolean. Measured so far (plain windowed, quad-layout): master Window Time ~0.48 s; worktree Window Time ~0.19-0.31 s, first paint ~1.0-1.5 s (AOT cache: first paint ~0.42 s).

Agent 2 startup cuts (wall profile of a plain windowed quad-layout run, 1 ms samples): audio device open moved off the main thread (Canvas3D.audioPlayMenuMusic and initGL audio init run via Platform.runInBackground, ~80 ms); AutomationRuntime class init moved into the background automation start (~65 ms; Canvas3D automation fields volatile, frames before it lands skip automation commands); startup-warm-up thread in IxdarWindow.main initializes org.lwjgl.opengl.GL (dlopen of libGL, ~110 ms) and CanvasSceneMap (loads all scene classes, ~100 ms) alongside GLFW's native start; ShaderType no longer compiles all 23 shader programs in its enum constructor, getShader compiles on first use (~85-100 ms). Machine load avg 13-19 from other agents makes timings noisy.

Agent 2: headless run-scene screenshots of quad-layout, cross-field-exam, mcg-exam, param-exam, embedded-tmesh, mesh-viewer, mesh-boolean, ring-tool are pixel-identical to master (image-diff identical=true; master captured from a git-archive build of 0f52d26f). Headless 'Time to First Paint' positive in all eight. Processing label falls back to the window title when a scene has no model path (mesh-boolean printed 'processing null'). Whole-suite run started: tmp/quad-suite/eng-14.

Agent 3 (DoD 2, plain windowed quad-layout, no debugger/profiler, 3 runs each, machine load ~7): worktree glfw init 0.10-0.14 s, Window Create 0.14-0.20 s, Window Time 0.15-0.22 s, Time to First Paint (after first glfwSwapBuffers, input mesh shown) 0.67, 0.72, 0.84 s. Master same runs: Window Time 0.35-0.38 s; its 'Time to First Paint' 0.59-0.64 s is printed before the frame and before QuadLayoutEngine runs, so it is not comparable. 0.1 s target not met; measured floor ~0.67 s. What is left (wall profile prof-3, main thread after Window Time): QuadLayoutScene/ModelScene constructor 0.12 s, Terminal init + clinit 0.15 s, Scene.initGL 0.10 s, initModel (mesh read + upload) 0.07 s, then the render thread's first frame ~0.2 s (shaders compiled on first use, fonts). A Java AOT cache (-XX:AOTCache) brought first paint to ~0.42 s in agent 2's runs; not wired into launch.json since the cache must be retrained after every build.

Agent 3 (DoD 6, the 0.49 s window gap): the gap is IxdarWindow.init from glfwCreateWindow to the 'Window Time' print. In a plain master run (wall profile base-wall.collapsed) it is 0.20 s, of which ManifoldMeshBooleanBackend.<clinit> loading the Manifold natives from LwjglPlatform's constructor is 0.15-0.16 s, the window icon decode (STBImage clinit + stbi_load) ~0.01 s, GL.createCapabilities 0.01 s, and glfwSetWindowPos raising GLFW_FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE on Wayland (with a printed stack trace) plus class loading the rest. The F5 entry's 0.49 s is the same work slowed by the JDWP debugger and async-profiler agents it attaches (class loading and JNI binding run instrumented). Worktree: Manifold backend built on first use, icon and window position skipped on Wayland, GL class init on the warm-up thread: the gap is now 0.01-0.02 s plain (Window Create 0.14 -> Window Time 0.15).

Agent 3: 'processing null' nit fixed. ModelScene.processInBackground names the job by the current model, else offPath, else windowTitle(); MeshBooleanScene now overrides windowTitle() ('Ixdar : Mesh Boolean', like its sibling scenes), so its label reads 'processing Ixdar : Mesh Boolean ... s' and its log 'processed Ixdar : Mesh Boolean in 0.19 s'. Headless mesh-boolean screenshot still pixel-identical to master.

Agent 3: the first eng-14 suite run was invalid. tmp/quad-suite/run_suite.py runs 'uv run --project <main Ixdar> ixdar-cli run-scene', and run_scene.py takes REPO_DIR from its own package path, so every mesh built and ran the main checkout (master 0f52d26f), whatever --checkout says. Its logs show master's negative headless first paint (-198000 s) and no 'processed' line. Its MATCHes (sphere_base..block) compared master with master. This affects every branch's suite results (craw-69 too). The master baseline itself is valid: main is clean at 0f52d26f. Rerun with a copy that passes --project <checkout> (scratchpad run_suite_checkout.py) into tmp/quad-suite/eng-14-worktree.

Round 2 item 1 (font atlas): new ixdar.graphics.render.text.FontAtlasBinary compiles msdf-atlas-gen's opensans.json + opensans.png into res/opensans.atlas (little-endian: magic IXFA, version, atlas size, px/em, distance range, em metrics as float64, 40-byte glyph rows already rounded the way Font used them, 12-byte kerning rows, then the texel crop rect and raw RGBA8 rows bottom-up; texels outside the crop are zero). 8,302,448 bytes vs 533 KB JSON+PNG: 1014 of 2048 atlas rows hold texels. Regenerate with 'mvn -q -pl ixdar-app exec:java@compile-font-atlas' (unbound exec execution); unit.text.FontAtlasBinaryTest fails when the committed binary is stale and checks the crop expands back to the PNG's texels exactly. Font reads it through new Platform.loadResourceBytes (desktop file, headless classpath) into one direct buffer: Font.<init> 105 ms -> 10 ms in the wall profile. Web returns null and keeps JSON+PNG (browser decodes the PNG natively and it is 17x smaller to download), but builds its glyph table through the same encoding, so there is one glyph rule. Text pixel-identical to master (quad-layout terminal screenshot, image-diff fuzz 0 identical=true).

Round 2 item 3 (initPoints): new Canvas3D.seedsUnitSquareShell (default true); ModelScene.initGL clears it, so initPoints skips the unit-square Shell (its PointND points are SDFCircles, its segments SDFLines, the DistanceMatrix and initShell) and frames Camera2D on an empty PointSet. Scene.initGL no longer calls initPoints a second time after Canvas3D.initGL already did (every Scene built its shell and Camera2D twice). Main-thread wall profile: initPoints 41 ms -> 4 ms. quad-layout terminal screenshot still pixel-identical to master (fuzz 0); arrow-line-canvas (a non-model Scene) matches master except its FPS counter.

Round 2 item 4 (mesh bounds): one upload scanned the HalfEdgeMesh 12 times (compileSurfaceData: boundsMin, boundsMax, center = 2 more, radius = 3 more; then frameMesh: center 2 + radius 3). Now compileSurfaceData derives the center from its min/max and calls new HalfEdgeMesh.radiusAbout(center) (radius() delegates to it, same arithmetic), and ModelScene.frameLoadedModel frames the orbit from the runtime's compiled center/radius (HalfEdgeMeshRuntime.compiledMesh now a public field; frameMesh split into frameMesh + frameOrbit(center, radius)): 3 scans per upload. Main-thread wall profile: bounds 26 ms -> 6 ms.

Round 2 item 2 (warm-up): startup-warm-up threads in IxdarWindow.main now also initialize JOML (Matrix4f.lookAt for Options' DecimalFormat, Matrix4d for MemUtil), the scene/command/geometry registries, PointND.Double and Arc (Terminal's initializer builds one of each geometry), the tool-package classes, the AutomationInputBinder.bind lookup, and the six GLFW callback interfaces (key, char, cursor, mouse button, scroll, window size) whose initializers build libffi CIFs. Main-thread wall profile: JOML Options 27 -> 0 ms, Terminal.<clinit> 51 -> 6 ms. LWJGL's own bootstrap (MemoryUtil/Library/MemoryStack inside Callback.<clinit>, ~70 ms) is the first thing main needs, so no thread can hide it: running it on main before starting the warm-ups was tried and measured worse (first paint median 0.662 vs 0.641 s, glfw init 0.128 vs 0.103 s) and removed. The leftover GL.coldStartStack (all three backends) and its MAT4_FLOATS constants are gone.

Round 2 item 5 (first swap): timed with temporary prints (removed) around the render thread's first frames, plain windowed quad-layout, 3-5 runs each. Wayland, swap interval 1: first glfwSwapBuffers 1-3 ms, second 0-3 ms, third 5-10 ms; the render thread starts at ~0.61 s and paints its first frame in ~25 ms. Swap interval 0 for the first swap: first swap 1-5 ms, first paint no better (median 0.692 vs 0.642 s, noise), so it was not kept. XWayland (temporary glfwInitHint GLFW_PLATFORM X11, removed): first swap 1-4 ms, first paint median 1.06 s (main-thread build slower; the Wayland-only icon/position skips do not apply). The ~130 ms Mesa EGL wait inside the first swap in the round-2 starting profile is no longer there: the compositor's measured share of first paint is 1-3 ms. Hyprland animations off could not be measured: 'hyprctl keyword animations:enabled 0' is refused by this Hyprland ('keyword can't work with non-legacy parsers. Use eval.'), so animations stayed on (getoption confirms true); no config file was touched and eval was not used without a ruling.

Round 2 verification: first paint (plain windowed quad-layout, Time to First Paint after the first glfwSwapBuffers) before round 2 0.685/0.758/0.800 s, median 0.758; after, at load ~6: median 0.622 (5 runs 0.603-0.679) and 0.641/0.642 in other 5-run sets; at load 12-15 the same build reads 0.69-0.88, so treat ~0.62-0.64 s as the figure. Main-thread wall profile before -> after: Font.<init> 102 -> 7 ms, initPoints 41 -> 2, mesh bounds 26 -> 7, JOML Options 27 -> 0, Terminal.<clinit> 51 -> 6-28, IxdarWindow.init 716 -> 531. Whole suite (tmp/quad-suite/eng-14-r2 vs master-0f52d26f): 12 MATCH; sphere_random and Hand-tri-30k DIFF are the known noise (image-diff max channel delta 1/255, 3 and 1 pixels at fuzz 0, 0 over fuzz 8); statuses and signatures all the same. FontAtlasBinaryTest 2/2 pass. wt done passed (launch entry 'ENG-14: quad-layout'); ticket REVIEW.

Round 3 (font atlas, 'compress to just what we use'): opensans.atlas is now version 2 (version byte) and 341,021 bytes, down from 8,302,448 (the source JSON + PNG are 533 KB, the PNG alone 489 KB). Layout, little-endian: int magic IXFA, byte version, u16 atlas width/height, float px/em, distance range, line height (em), ascender (px, precomputed with Font's arithmetic; the unread descender and em doubles are gone); u16 glyph count + 30-byte rows (char, u16 x/y/w/h, float advance + plane bounds); int kerning count + 8-byte rows (char, char, float); u16 tile count + one u16 x/y/w/h tile per glyph; then one Deflater level-9 stream of the tiles' RGB rows. Channels: only RGB, since sdf.fs takes median(r,g,b) and never reads alpha (the atlas is mtsdf; its alpha is dropped); Texture.rgbOnly uploads GL_RGB8/GL_RGB with GL_UNPACK_ALIGNMENT 1 (new GL.RGB/RGB8/unpackAlignment in the lwjgl, headless and web backends). Texels: each glyph's whole texel box (floor/ceil of atlasBounds, which sit half a texel inside it; bilinear sampling at a glyph edge reads that half); the converter refuses an atlas with a non-zero texel outside every box, so the texture's size, the glyph UVs and every texel are unchanged and the rest is zero. Each tile row after its first is stored as its byte difference from the row below (PNG's Up filter): 337 KB at level 9 vs 946 KB unfiltered; level 9 inflates no slower than 1-6 here, so the smallest was kept. Font.<init> (1 ms wall profile, plain windowed quad-layout, main thread): median 27 ms over 5 runs (23-28, one outlier 50 on a cold file read), vs 7 ms for round 2's raw binary and 102 ms for the old JSON+PNG path; ~7 ms is the inflate and ~15 ms the cold-JVM un-filter loop (done eight bytes per step). Also fixed: the resources include list had no *.atlas, so the headless classpath never had the binary and headless silently used JSON+PNG; it now takes the binary (decodeTexels in a headless profile). Text pixel-identical to master fe23ca3e (craw-68): quad-layout terminal screenshot after 'help', image-diff fuzz 0 identical=true, same sha256. FontAtlasBinaryTest 2/2: the committed binary's metadata must match the JSON byte for byte and its texels must inflate to the PNG's RGB exactly (compared after inflating, so another zlib's deflate bytes do not read as stale), and a fresh encoding must expand to the PNG's RGB. TeaVM web build OK (web still loads JSON + PNG).
